key_insight: Engine position noticeably changes early contrail and vortex-wake evolution, but these differences mostly fade as atmospheric conditions and vortex dynamics take over.
engineering_relevance: For aircraft designers, engine placement matters most for near-field contrail formation and early wake behavior, with limited long-time impact on contrail microphysics in the tested cases.
method: 3D Large Eddy Simulations on a realistic aircraft geometry
Eulerian bulk microphysical model for contrail particles
Initialized from prior RANS fields; tested 3 engine positions under 2 stratifications and 2 humidity levels
evidence_signal: The abstract reports comparative simulation results across three engine placements, showing altered vortex instability timing, vortex-pair descent, and particle distribution, while contrail properties converge later in time.
watch_item: Results are specific to the simulated aircraft, atmospheric stratifications, and humidity cases studied, so broader generalization should be made cautiously.
paper_title: Engine position effects on contrail evolution for a realistic aircraft configuration
